children: Shares of Charter Communications Inc. (CHTR) jumped by over 8% on Wednesday, posting a second consecutive day of gains as sentiment around the stock improved.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment jumped from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours, a marked improvement from the ‘bearish’ territory it was in a week ago.
Retail Traders Turn Bullish On CHTR Stock
Retail chatter around
jumped 154%, according to platform data.
One bullish user
, “$CHTR The gift that keeps on giving…”
Another user
, “$CHTR Nice decisive break through the $140 resistance level.” Shares of the company closed at $147.27 on Wednesday.

However, a third user pointed out, “$CHTR has $108B in debt, a junk credit rating, shrinking broadband market share and $42B of debt maturing through 2031. It must compete with AI for capital while fighting fiber, T-Mobile and Starlink for customers. Zero cash dividends. A leveraged bet on a deteriorating franchise. All it has going for it is a low PE due to the massive leverage.”
CHTR Stock: Q3 Results Snapshot
Earlier this month, Charter Communications posted its third-quarter results, reporting revenue of $14.92 billion, up 9.1% year-over-year, and a GAAP diluted loss per share of $20.50.
The company’s top-line growth was boosted by the closing of the Cox Communications acquisition, while the bottom-line loss was primarily driven by a non-cash $6.3 billion franchise impairment charge.
Charter ended the quarter with $573 million in cash and cash equivalents against $109.93 billion in total debt.

Meanwhile, total customer relationships stood at 36.7 million, down 1.8% year-on-year. Internet subscribers also fell by a pro forma net loss of 233,000 to 34.3 million, while video subscribers dropped by 77,000 to 13.8 million.
However, the company’s mobile lines expanded 15% year-over-year to 13.5 million, strengthened by 508,000 net new pro forma lines added during the quarter.
CHTR stock is down more than 29% year-to-date.
